title: Send Across the Await
goal: The future holds a counter across an .await — and must stay Send. Choose the counter that can cross threads.
hints: A future remembers every local it holds across an .await — those locals ARE the future's state.
Rc's reference count isn't atomic, so an Rc-holding future can't be Send. Arc is the thread-safe twin.
explanation: requires_send stands in for tokio::spawn: multithreaded executors demand Send futures. The future's state is whatever lives across an .await — hold an Rc there and the entire future becomes !Send (E0277, with the compiler pointing at exactly which value and which await). Arc is the atomic twin: same sharing, Send-safe, future crosses threads freely. This diagnosis — 'future is not Send, held across await' — is the single most common async compile error in real Rust; now you can read it. (Cell<i32> is Send too — but it isn't a pointer: there's nothing to deref, E0614. Wrappers earn their place by what they provide.)
